title: Resource management & lifetime
literature: Stroustrup / Meyers Effective C++ (RAII, smart pointers); Alexandrescu Modern C++ Design; pool/arena literature; Preschern 'Fluent C' resource patterns.

members.name: Allocation Wrapper
members.what: Wrap the raw allocation/deallocation calls (malloc/free) in your own functions so every allocation flows through one place that can check for failure, add statistics, tagging, debugging hooks, or alternative backing allocators.

members.name: Asset Streaming
members.what: The engine loads and unloads game assets (geometry, textures, audio, world chunks) asynchronously in the background, keyed to player position or predicted need, keeping only a sliding working set resident within a memory budget.

members.name: Boundary Tags
members.what: Size/status fields at both ends of each heap block let an allocator find and merge free neighbors in constant time on free.

members.name: Buddy Memory Allocation
members.what: Manage memory in power-of-two-sized blocks that split into two 'buddies' on allocation and coalesce back with their buddy on free, found by address arithmetic.

members.name: Bulkhead
members.what: Partition resources (thread pools, connection pools, memory) into isolated compartments per client or function so one compartment's exhaustion cannot sink the rest.

members.name: Callee Allocates
members.what: The callee allocates the result buffer (of size only it knows) and returns it with a paired deallocation function the caller must invoke.

members.name: Caller-Owned Buffer
members.what: The caller allocates and owns the buffer, passing pointer and size for the callee to fill.

members.name: Captain Oates
members.what: On memory pressure, have less vital components voluntarily sacrifice their memory (caches, optional buffers) so more important tasks can proceed.

members.name: Compaction
members.what: Move live objects together in memory to squeeze out the unused gaps between them, recovering memory lost to fragmentation.

members.name: Component Configurator
members.what: An application links and unlinks component implementations at runtime via a uniform component lifecycle interface (init, suspend, resume, fini) and a central configurator, without recompiling or restarting.

members.name: Copy-on-Write
members.what: Share an object between clients until one needs to modify it, then transparently copy it and let the writer mutate the private copy.

members.name: Custom Allocator
members.what: Containers and subsystems take an allocator object/parameter so memory sourcing policy is chosen by the client, not hard-coded.

members.name: Data Files
members.what: Process data a little at a time from secondary storage, keeping only the current working portion in main memory.

members.name: Dedicated Ownership
members.what: Every allocation is assigned exactly one owner responsible for freeing it, with ownership transfer made explicit at API boundaries.

members.name: Dispose Pattern
members.what: Objects owning unmanaged resources expose an explicit Dispose/close method, invoked deterministically via language constructs (using / try-with-resources), with finalizers only as backstop.

members.name: Eager Acquisition
members.what: Resources are acquired up front, before actual use (at startup or configuration time), and handed out from the pre-acquired set at run time.

members.name: Epoch-Based Reclamation
members.what: Threads announce a global epoch on entering read-side sections; retired nodes are freed only after all threads have advanced past the epoch in which the nodes were retired.

members.name: Evictor
members.what: An evictor monitors resource usage and, under a configurable strategy (LRU, LFU, priorities), releases or swaps out the least valuable resources to bound consumption.

members.name: Execute Around Method
members.what: A method (or scoped object) performs guaranteed paired actions - acquire/release, open/close, begin/end - around a client-supplied block of code.

members.name: Fixed Sized Buffer
members.what: Allocate memory only in one (or a few) fixed sizes - sized for the worst case - so freed blocks are always exactly reusable.

members.name: Free List
members.what: Linked list threaded through unused memory blocks or object slots themselves, from which an allocator pops on allocate and onto which it pushes on free.

members.name: Garbage Collection
members.what: A runtime mechanism that finds no-longer-referenced allocations and reclaims (and, in compacting variants, relocates) them without explicit frees.

members.name: GC Read Barrier
members.what: A small check or fixup executed on every (or selected) pointer load so a concurrent or moving collector can intercept reads of stale or unforwarded references.

members.name: GC Write Barrier
members.what: A small code sequence the compiler or runtime inserts on every pointer store that records or checks the mutated reference (e.g. by marking a card in a card table or appending to a remembered set), so the collector can find cross-generation

members.name: Hazard Pointers
members.what: Each thread publishes single-writer pointers naming the nodes it is currently accessing; reclaimers defer freeing any node named in a hazard pointer.

members.name: Hooks
members.what: Access read-only information through hooks (pointers or jump slots) held in writable storage, so changing the hooks gives the illusion of changing ROM content.

members.name: Lazy Cleanup
aka: let the OS reclaim at exit
members.what: Deliberately never free dynamically allocated memory whose lifetime spans the whole program run, relying on the operating system to reclaim it at process exit.

members.name: Leasing
members.what: A resource is granted for a limited time; the holder must renew the lease to keep it, and expiry releases the resource automatically.

members.name: List Virtualization
members.what: Renders only the subset of a long scrollable list that is visible in the viewport (plus a small buffer), creating, recycling, and repositioning a fixed pool of item views as the user scrolls.

members.name: Lookup
members.what: Resource providers register references with a lookup service under known names or properties; users query the service to find and access the resources.

members.name: Memory Arena
members.what: Allocate objects by bumping a pointer through a large block and free them all at once by resetting or discarding the whole arena.

members.name: Memory Discard
members.what: Allocate temporary objects from a temporary workspace and reclaim them all at once by discarding the whole workspace.

members.name: Memory Limit
members.what: Set an explicit memory budget for each component and fail allocations that would exceed the component's limit.

members.name: Memory Overlay
members.what: Divide a program into sections that share the same memory region, loading each overlay from secondary storage into the shared region only when its code/data is needed.

members.name: Object Manager
members.what: A manager component separate from both clients and managed objects controls the objects' creation, access, and destruction, issuing references while owning the lifecycle.

members.name: Paging
members.what: Keep code and data on secondary storage and move fixed-size pages in and out of main memory on demand, giving the illusion of more memory.

members.name: Partial Acquisition
members.what: A large resource is acquired in stages - only the part needed now, with further parts acquired progressively (e.g. lazy-loading pages of an image or file).

members.name: Pool Allocation
members.what: Pre-allocated pools of fixed-size blocks (often one pool per object type/size) from which objects are checked out and returned in O(1).

members.name: Pooling
members.what: Released resources are recycled into a pool and handed out again on demand, amortizing acquisition/release cost across many uses; the pool manages size and eviction.

members.name: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization)
members.what: Tie a resource's lifetime to an object's lifetime so acquisition happens in the constructor and release happens deterministically in the destructor at scope exit.

members.name: Read-Only Memory
members.what: Place read-only code and constant data in ROM/flash rather than RAM, reserving scarce writable memory for mutable state.

members.name: Reference Counting
members.what: A handle class embeds a reference counter in (or beside) a dynamically allocated body object, updating it on copy/assignment/destruction and deleting the body when the count reaches zero.

members.name: Resource Files
members.what: Keep configuration data and read-only resources in files on secondary storage, loading and discarding each item as needed.

members.name: Resource Lifecycle Manager
members.what: A dedicated manager component centrally controls the whole lifecycle of a class of resources - acquisition, coordination, optimization, and release - decoupling lifecycle from resource use.

members.name: Rule of Three/Five/Zero
members.what: If a class defines any of destructor/copy/move special members it should deliberately define the whole set (three/five) - or own no resources directly and define none (zero).

members.name: Scope Guard
members.what: An ad-hoc RAII object that runs an arbitrary cleanup or rollback action when a scope exits, optionally dismissible on success.

members.name: Sharing
members.what: Store one copy of identical information and reference it from everywhere it is needed instead of duplicating it.

members.name: Slab Allocator
members.what: Carve memory into per-type slabs of preconstructed, fixed-size objects and cache freed objects in initialized state for immediate reuse.

members.name: Small Buffer Optimization
members.what: A container or wrapper embeds a small fixed-size buffer inside itself and only falls back to heap allocation when contents exceed it.

members.name: Smart Pointer
members.what: A pointer-like object that wraps a raw pointer, validity-checks access, and manages the pointee's lifetime (typically by reference counting), releasing it when the last reference disappears.

members.name: Stack First
members.what: Default data placement on the call stack (automatic storage), reaching for static or heap storage only when lifetime or size demands it.

members.name: Static Allocation
members.what: All objects and buffers are allocated at compile/link time or once at startup, and the heap is never used afterwards.

members.name: Steady State
members.what: For every mechanism that accumulates a resource (log files, cache entries, rows, temp files), pair a mechanism that recycles or purges it, so the program can run indefinitely without human cleanup.

members.name: Two-Level Segregated Fit Allocator (TLSF)
members.what: A dynamic allocator using a two-level bitmap-indexed segregated-fit structure giving O(1) worst-case malloc and free.

members.name: Variable Allocation
members.what: Allocate and deallocate variable-sized objects on demand from a heap as the program needs them.

members.name: Weak Reference
members.what: A reference that does not keep its target alive: it can be dereferenced only while the target still exists and observably lapses when the target is reclaimed.
